grades.reason: A reviewer reports their child was threatened by a person in an 'adopt me' game and police took the predator into custody. Another reviewer says a 40-50 year old man tried to meet up with a child using the app. Researchers using under-13 accounts reported encountering sexual references and offensive language within minutes. Fairplay and NCOSE said Roblox's voice and text chat features facilitate predation by enabling adult contact with minors. Forum users report that even with chat set to 'no one,' mini-games with built-in chat cannot be disabled, and chatting on 'signs' lets kids bypass parental controls.

A source names a purchase control that answers this concern (Set a spending limit), and no verified quote says the control failed or was bypassed. Complaints about spending, scams or billing are not counted against it.

A reviewer reports 'if a four year old does it and it says that they are twenty five then what do they do.' Another reviewer says their child was placed in the '28th group.' A reviewer contacting support was told to wait until age 13, but the system showed a birthday of Oct 7, 1985, stating they were 41 while they were younger than 13.

Reviewers report role-play games like Brookhaven involve 'disturbing and inappropriate stuff' and 'online dating.' A forum user describes a 'Baddies' game labeled 5+ that encouraged punching, stomping, and shooting in the opening tutorial. Another forum quote says a 'Street Code' game showed an intense fiery car accident and prompted the player to decide whether to shoot or save an officer within seconds.
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton says he has sued Roblox over 'flagrantly ignoring' safety laws and 'deceiving parents' about the dangers the platform poses to young people.
